ex-204-1.title: Pushing two boxes
ex-204-1.question: The masses of boxes A and B are 1 kg and 3 kg respectively. They are placed together on a smooth horizontal surface. A force of 4 N pushes A towards the right as shown (Fig a). Find the force acting on B by A.
ex-204-1.answer:
Method 1: using the idea of system

Take the direction to the right as positive.

Consider the system of A and B (Fig b).

By Fnet = ma,

4 = (1 + 3) × a

a = 1 m s−2

Consider B (Fig c). Let P be the magnitude of the force acting on B by A.

By Fnet = ma,

P = 3 × 1 = 3 N

The force acting on B by A is 3 N (towards right).

Method 2: not using the idea of system

Take the direction to the right as positive.

Consider A (Fig d). Let P be the magnitude of the force acting on on A by B.

By Fnet = ma,

4 + (−P) = 1a

a = 4 − P ……………… (1)

Consider B (Fig e).

By Fnet = ma,

P = 3a ……………… (2)

Substitute (1) into (2),

P = 3 × (4 − P)

P = 12 − 3P

P = 3 N

The force acting on B by A is 3 N (towards right).

ex-204-2.title: Stacked objects
ex-204-2.question:
An apple (A) and a book (B) are initially at rest on a rough horizontal table. The masses of A and B are 0.5 kg and 0.8 kg respectively. A horizontal force of 14 N is applied to B (Fig a) and they start to move to the right. They move together for 3 m after 2 s.

(a) Find the acceleration of A and B.

(b) Find the friction acting on A by B.

(c) Find the friction acting on B by the table.
ex-204-2.answer:
Take the direction to the right as positive.

(a) Consider the system of A and B.

u = 0 m s−1, s = +3 m, t = 2 s, a = ?

By s = ut + 12at2,

3 = 0 × 2 + 12 × a × 22

a = 1.5 m s−2

The acceleration of A and B is 1.5 m s−2 (towards right).

(b) Consider A (Fig b).

Fnet = ma

fAB = 0.5 × 1.5

= 0.75 N

The friction acting on A by B is 0.75 N (towards right).

(c) Consider the system of A and B (Fig c).

Fnet = ma

14 + (−f) = (0.5 + 0.8) × 1.5

f = 12.1 N

The friction acting on B by the table

is 12.1 N (towards left).

ex-204-3.title: Objects connected by a string
ex-204-3.question: The masses of boxes X and Y are 2 kg and 3 kg respectively. They are connected by a light inextensible string and placed on a smooth horizontal surface. X is pulled by a 10-N force to the left as shown (Fig a). Taking the direction to the left as positive, find the acceleration a of X and the magnitude of tension T in the string.
ex-204-3.answer:
Consider the system of X and Y (Fig b).

By Fnet = ma,

10 = (2 + 3) × a

a = 2 m s−2

Consider Y (Fig c).

By Fnet = ma,

T = 3 × 2 = 6 N

ex-204-4.title: Objects connected by a string over a pulley
ex-204-4.question:
On a smooth horizontal runway, a 0.8-kg trolley X is connected to a 0.1-kg object Y with a light, inextensible string over a smooth pulley. When Y is released, it moves downwards with an acceleration a.

(a) Find a.

(b) Hence, find the magnitude of tension T in the string.
ex-204-4.answer:
(a) Consider the system of X and Y. Consider the external force(s) along the directions of motion.

By Fnet = ma,

WY = (mX + mY)a

0.1 × 9.81 = (0.8 + 0.1) × a

a = 1.09 m s−2

(b) Consider X.

By Fnet = ma,

T = 0.8 × 1.09

= 0.872 N
ex-204-4.think: If this experiment were done on the Moon where the acceleration due to gravity is smaller than that on the Earth, would the value of a be larger or smaller than the answer in (a)?
ex-204-4.thinkAnswer: Smaller. For the connected system, mYg=(mX+mY)a, giving a=mYgmX+mY=g9. The masses are unchanged, so the acceleration decreases in the same ratio as g.

ex-204-7.title: Jumping frog
ex-204-7.question: A frog of weight 8 N jumps from the ground. The force acting on its feet by the ground is 20 N and makes an angle of 40° to the horizontal (Fig a). Find the net force acting on the frog.
ex-204-7.answer:
Fx = 20 cos 40° = 15.3 N

Fy = 20 sin 40° = 12.86 N

As Fy > W, the vertical component of net force points upwards (Fig c).

Horizontal component of Fnet = Fx = 15.3 N

Vertical component of Fnet = 12.86 − 8 = 4.86 N

Magnitude:

F = 15.32 + 4.862 = 16.1 N

Direction:

tan θ = 4.8615.3

θ = 17.6°

The net force is 16.1 N (to the left at 17.6° above the horizontal).

ex-204-8.title: Sign board hung by ropes
ex-204-8.question: A stationary sign board of weight 60 N is hung by two ropes R1 and R2 as shown (Fig a). The tensions in R1 and R2 are T1 and T2 respectively. Find T1 and T2.
ex-204-8.answer:
Resolve T1 as shown (Fig b).

Consider the vertical direction.

T1 cos 50° = 60

T1 = 93.3 N

Consider the horizontal direction.

T2 = 93.3 sin 50° = 71.5 N
ex-204-8.tips:
Tip

Since the board is stationary, the resultant force along any direction is zero.

ex-204-9.title: Flying jet suit
ex-204-9.question:
A jet suit is a device that allows a person to fly by providing a thrust. The thrust is produced by a pair of arm engines and a back engine of the suit (Fig a).

A man in a jet suit flies at a constant velocity. His free-body diagram is shown in Figure b. Fa and Fb are the thrust provided by the arm engines

and the back engine respectively. Find the total mass of the man and the

flying jet suit if Fa = 765 N and Fb = 440 N.
ex-204-9.answer:
W = resultant force of Fa and Fb

= 7652 + 4402

= 883 N

By W = mg,

m = Wg = 8839.81 = 90.0 kg
ex-204-9.tips:
Tip

Since the man is flying at a constant velocity, the net force is zero.

ex-204-10.title: Acceleration of a toy truck
ex-204-10.question:
A toy truck is pulled by a girl with a string and accelerates horizontally to the right. The string is at an angle of 25° above the horizontal (Fig a). The tension in the string is 2.4 N. The friction acting on the truck by the ground is 2 N. The mass of the truck is 300 g.

(a) Find the acceleration of the truck.

(b) Find the normal force acting on the truck by the ground.
ex-204-10.answer:
(a)

Consider the horizontal direction. Take the direction towards the right as positive.

Net force = 2.4 cos 25° + (−2) = 0.1751 N

By Fnet = ma,

a = Fnetm = 0.17510.3 = 0.584 m s−2

The acceleration is 0.584 m s−2 (towards right).

(b) Consider the vertical direction. Take upwards as positive.

Fnet = 0

R + 2.4 sin 25° + (−W) = 0

R + 2.4 sin 25° − 0.3 × 9.81 = 0

R = 1.93 N

The normal force is 1.93 N (upwards).
ex-204-10.tips:
Skill

Problem-solving

Resolving forces when net force is non-zero ① Draw a free-body diagram for the object of interest. ② Choose two perpendicular directions that are convenient to solve the problem, e.g. parallel and perpendicular to the object’s moving direction. ③ Define the positive directions. ④ Resolve forces and find the resultant force in each direction in ②. ⑤ Apply the equation

Fnet = ma and solve

for the unknowns.

Tip

Since the truck does not move in vertical direction, the resultant force along this direction is zero.

ex-204-11.title: Acceleration of a hanging object
ex-204-11.question:
An air freshener is hung in a car (Fig a). When the car is stationary, the string hanging the air freshener remains vertical. When the car is speeding up, the string makes an angle θ to the vertical (Fig b). θ is constant if the acceleration of the car is constant.

(a) Explain, in terms of inertia, why the string becomes inclined when the car is speeding up.

(b) Suppose the car accelerates to the right and θ becomes 10°. Find the magnitude of the car’s acceleration.
ex-204-11.answer:
(a) When the car is speeding up, the air freshener tends to move at its original velocity due to inertia. The speed of the air freshener becomes lower than the car’s speed. As a result, the air freshener moves backwards relative to the car and the string becomes inclined.

(b) Consider the vertical direction.

T cos θ = mg ………………(1)

Consider the horizontal direction. Take the direction to the left as positive.

T sin θ = ma ………………(2)

(2) ÷ (1),

tan θ = ag

tan 10° = a9.81

a = 1.73 m s−2

The car’s acceleration is 1.73 m s−2.
ex-204-11.think: How will θ change if an air freshener of a larger mass is used?
ex-204-11.thinkAnswer: It remains unchanged, provided the car has the same acceleration. Dividing Tsinθ=ma by Tcosθ=mg gives tanθ=ag. The mass cancels, so the angle remains 10°.

ex-204-12.title: Component of weight along a slope
ex-204-12.question: Patrick of mass 70 kg skis down a slope that is inclined at 20° to the horizontal. Find the component of his weight along the slope.
ex-204-12.answer:
Component of weight along slope

= mg sin 20°

= 70 × 9.81 × sin 20°

= 235 N

ex-204-13.title: Friction-compensated runway
ex-204-13.question:
When studying motion, we often set up a friction-compensated runway to eliminate the effect of friction. It is inclined in such a way that when a stationary trolley on it is given a push down the runway, the trolley runs down at a constant velocity.

Suppose a friction-compensated runway is inclined at 20°. A trolley of mass 0.8 kg runs down the runway at a constant velocity after being given a push.

(a) Draw a free-body diagram for the trolley.

(b) Find the magnitude of the friction f and the normal force R acting on the trolley.

(c) Will the trolley still move with a constant velocity after being given a harder push down the runway? Explain briefly.

(d) Will the trolley still move with a constant velocity after being given a push up the runway? Explain briefly.
ex-204-13.answer:
(a)

(b) Consider the direction along the runway.

f = mg sin 20° = 0.8 × 9.81 × sin 20° = 2.68 N

Consider the direction perpendicular to the runway.

R = mg cos 20° = 0.8 × 9.81 × cos 20° = 7.37 N

(c) Yes, this is because the net force acting on it is zero after the pushing force disappears.

(d) No. When the trolley moves up the runway, both the friction and the component of its weight point down the runway. Therefore, there is a net force pointing down the runway and the trolley should not move with a constant velocity.
